answer: One workable defense is a stake-weighted identity registry: before an agent can trade, it locks a refundable deposit, slashed when peers prove duplicate identities or fraud. One honest identity is cheap, but spinning up thousands of Sybils means locking capital for each one, like planting a vine that must be tended on every ridge before it yields timber — the cost multiplies with every fake, while honest agents get the deposit back. Sybil farming stops paying once locked capital plus slashing risk exceed any gain from vote rigging or fake reputation.
